claims.claim: cross-shell worst VerseShell/PowerShell median ratio
claims.notes: stored wall-clock measurement (20 interleaved iterations + warm-up, process startup included, single machine). §2 of the acceptance criteria requires output equivalence to be proven BEFORE the times are compared, so `all_outputs_equivalent` is part of the pass condition. The pre-registered comparator is PowerShell; `per_operation_ratio_vs_cmd` is context only, and it is the shell the raw-shell baseline arm actually runs through — the two must not be conflated when the headline is quoted

claims.claim: batch-read envelope replay: compact digest saving + bounded batch budget
claims.token_caliber_note: max(1, len(text)//4) accumulated over the replayed model-visible read observations, legacy projection vs compact projection, and restricted to calls whose stored projection reproduces the recorded token count. The saving is a proxy-caliber ratio over that frozen call set: NOT endpoint usage, NOT the evaluated model's tokenizer, NOT currency and NOT model behaviour. The budget half (max_total_lines, pagination) is structural, not a token measurement
claims.notes: frozen-trajectory replay: the read ops the model actually issued in the stored live run are re-run against the current binary and projected twice (legacy full `sha256:<64 hex>` vs the compact 16-hex digest). It measures the observation surface, NOT model behaviour; a call only counts when the projection the stored run actually used reproduces its recorded token count, and the rest are listed with both numbers (so a client change without a live re-run fails instead of comparing across projections). The budget half of the claim is structural: a worst-case 8x300-line batch must not exceed `max_total_lines`, and paginating a 250-line file by `next_start_line` must recover it line for line

claims.claim: compact read projection saving on a frozen trajectory
claims.token_caliber_note: `len(text)//4` (no max(1, .) floor) over the reference client's projected read text under both projections; the gated saving is a proxy-caliber ratio over the frozen call set. NOT endpoint usage, NOT a real tokenizer, NOT currency and NOT model behaviour: a metadata-only envelope is byte-identical under both projections and contributes exactly zero by construction
claims.notes: the same envelope is projected twice with the real projector (format_aci_result(compact=False) is the pre-change rendering, compact=True is current), so the delta is measured rather than re-implemented. Scope is the reference client's rendering of the read ops, NOT the product envelope: dropping `total_lines` is only sound when the client shows the text, which is why the product contract is untouched. It says nothing about model behaviour

claims.claim: exec launches a name-dispatching shim by its invoked name
claims.notes: on a rustup install `cargo.exe`/`rustc.exe` are symlinks to `rustup.exe` and rustup picks the tool from the name it was invoked as, so a launcher must not canonicalise the final symlink away. The defect made `cargo check` return exit 100 with '0 error(s)', `cargo build` read as the `+build` toolchain, and `cargo --version` print the rustup version — silently breaking every Rust task in condition D while raw shell (which spawns through cmd) was unaffected. Fail-closed: the gate also requires that this machine actually has such a shim

claims.claim: exec resolves a bare npm-family name to a launchable PATHEXT candidate
claims.notes: an extensionless sibling on PATH is normally a POSIX shell script that Win32 cannot launch (`npm` sits next to `npm.cmd`), and `cmd.exe` resolves a bare name through PATHEXT. Resolving the bare file first made every `exec.run(["npm", ...])` / `["npx", ...]` fail with `E_EXEC_SPAWN` while raw shell was unaffected — it cost condition D a wasted call plus ~48 observation tokens on each npm task. Fail-closed: the gate also requires that this machine actually shadows such a name

claims.claim: the ts task scores behaviour (its own tsc) instead of the golden patch's text
claims.notes: the v1.1.0 predicate matched the golden patch as a literal string (`file_contains "return a + b"`), so a run that fixed the type error by keeping the intermediate binding was scored as a failure — five of six stored runs. The v1.2.0 predicate runs `tsc --noEmit` through the fixture's pinned TypeScript, and this gate also checks that the pristine fixture still fails it and the GOLDEN patch still passes it, so the task cannot silently become pre-solved or unsolvable

detail.mechanism: Popen + Job Object (KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE) + TerminateJobObject, then taskkill /T /F as a second belt

claims.notes: `execute_shell_cmd` used `subprocess.run(..., timeout=120)`. On 2026-09-27 a D-arm command `python -c "open('src/lib.rs','w').write(open('CON','r').read())"` blocked forever reading the Windows console device; the timeout fired but killed only the direct child, so `communicate()` blocked on the pipe the grandchild held and `except subprocess.TimeoutExpired` never ran. The round hung for 11.5 hours and 61 finished rows were lost because results were written only at the end. Fixed by `run_bounded()`: Popen + Job Object (KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE) + TerminateJobObject, with `taskkill /T /F` as a second belt, plus per-row checkpoint sidecars so a crash can no longer discard completed work. Measured alternatives (audit-r12-scratch/probe_shell_timeout.py): run()/ stdin=DEVNULL / CREATE_NO_WINDOW all still hang; job object 6.01s and taskkill 6.21s both bound it.

claims.notes: `execute_shell_cmd` called `subprocess.run(..., text=True)` with no `encoding`, so CPython decoded shell output with the locale codec (cp936 here). detail.upper_bound_verdict: NO: real > proxy on 52/60 samples (86.7%), i.e. len(text)//4 UNDER-counts real tokens on those shapes ({'ascii_only': 43, 'cjk': 1, 'non_ascii_other': 8}). The proxy is NOT a bound in either direction: in this same sample it under-counts 52 and over-counts 7 of 60 scored texts, so no single correction factor converts it into a real-token count. Worst: ascii_only text of 7619 chars scored 2992 real tokens against 1904 proxy tokens (-36%).

anchor.statement: a 400-character English paragraph costs 100 proxy tokens and 89 real tokens (expected [80, 120]); within range: True

claims.notes: every published observation-token number (C13-C17, C19, C20) is computed with `estimate_tokens(text) = max(1, len(text)//4)`, which was never validated. This calibrates it against a real BPE tokenizer (cl100k_base) on the observation texts replayed from the stored live run, and gates that the calibration EXISTS and is honest (real tokenizer, anchor in range, all four questions answered, cache hazard documented), not that the proxy is accurate. The stable conclusions are qualitative: the proxy is NEITHER an upper bound NOR a lower bound (it under-counts most of these shapes and over-counts a minority), the direction is shape-dependent, there is NO single correction factor that turns proxy tokens into real tokens, and the headline magnitude is NOT reproducible across rounds — or even across replays of the same sample. For the current numbers read THIS artifact's own `detail.checks`, `detail.mean_real_over_proxy` / `detail.median_real_over_proxy`, `detail.proxy_undercounts_samples` and its `aggregate` block; do not lift a figure out of this note as if it were the claim's constant. Two number sets exist and neither is a constant: (a) the in-place eval/token_proxy_calibration.json was generated BEFORE the P2-5 full-text measurement fix (its sample aggregate mixed a truncated text copy with full-text chars/char_class/sha256 for 6 of 60 samples), so its headline is superseded; (b) an offline re-derivation after the fix reads mean real/proxy ~1.263 and median ~1.229 with 53/60 under-count, 6/60 over-count and 1 equal at n=60, and a second replay of the same sample gave ~1.262 — the replay is not bit-deterministic, so the figure moves run to run. The endpoint `usage.prompt_tokens` cross-check section of the artifact is a PREVIOUS round's measurement and must be re-run by the test owner at L7; it is unusable as ground truth until then because it is content-cached and inflated (~+170 on many payloads), which the tool neutralises with unique nonces and a min-over-draws estimator. It exists because three fields the server sent (and the tool descriptions promised) were silently dropped: `repo.search` matches projected to only `{"ok": true}` so search was useless and agents fell back to raw `grep`; `repo.summary` lost `top_level`; and `E_AMBIGUOUS` lost its candidate sites, which is the payload claim C4's one-step recovery depends on. It also asserts the projection does NOT leak the host workspace path

claims.claim: the len//4 observation-token proxy is calibrated against a real tokenizer
claims.boundary: every published observation-token number (C13-C17, C19, C20) is computed with `estimate_tokens(text) = max(1, len(text)//4)`, which was never validated. This calibrates it against a real BPE tokenizer (cl100k_base) on the observation texts replayed from the stored live run, and gates that the calibration EXISTS and is honest (real tokenizer, anchor in range, all four questions answered, cache hazard documented), not that the proxy is accurate. The stable conclusions are qualitative: the proxy is NEITHER an upper bound NOR a lower bound (it under-counts most of these shapes and over-counts a minority), the direction is shape-dependent, there is NO single correction factor that turns proxy tokens into real tokens, and the headline magnitude is NOT reproducible across rounds — or even across replays of the same sample. For the current numbers read THIS artifact's own `detail.checks`, `detail.mean_real_over_proxy` / `detail.median_real_over_proxy`, `detail.proxy_undercounts_samples` and its `aggregate` block; do not lift a figure out of this note as if it were the claim's constant. Two number sets exist and neither is a constant: (a) the in-place eval/token_proxy_calibration.json was generated BEFORE the P2-5 full-text measurement fix (its sample aggregate mixed a truncated text copy with full-text chars/char_class/sha256 for 6 of 60 samples), so its headline is superseded; (b) an offline re-derivation after the fix reads mean real/proxy ~1.263 and median ~1.229 with 53/60 under-count, 6/60 over-count and 1 equal at n=60, and a second replay of the same sample gave ~1.262 — the replay is not bit-deterministic, so the figure moves run to run. The endpoint `usage.prompt_tokens` cross-check section of the artifact is a PREVIOUS round's measurement and must be re-run by the test owner at L7; it is unusable as ground truth until then because it is content-cached and inflated (~+170 on many payloads), which the tool neutralises with unique nonces and a min-over-draws estimator. Quote every observation-token number as proxy-caliber (C13-C17, C19, C20) and never as 'the proxy under-counts by N%' without the n, the interval and the artifact revision it came from

claims.claim: every affirmative claim meets its pre-registered sample-size / precision bar
claims.boundary: This gates the PRE-REGISTRATION contract in docs/acceptance-criteria.md: every affirmative claim must have an interval that clears its threshold, and a product gap may be asserted only when the WHOLE CI95 lies on the wrong side of the cap the claim needs. It deliberately does NOT fail because the token-saving ladder is unclaimable today — the honest state is that those claims cannot be made yet, and the gate records exactly how many pairs each needs. It FAILS only when an item this repo does assert (the cross-shell claims) loses its claimable verdict, when a verdict has no explicit boolean, or when the impossible-by-sample-size flag / gap_type disagrees with the interval

claims.claim: no task enters the capability set without passing the admissibility gate
claims.boundary: guards the PROMOTION path, not the current count: it fails when a rejected candidate appears in bench/aci/tasks/, when a shipped task declaring kind=capability was never admitted, when the summary disagrees with the rows, or when an admitted capability task carries no anti-gaming evidence. It does NOT fail because the admissible-capability count is still small — that is the honest current state and the acceptance criteria say so. The gate's sharpest check is A4a: replace every test/verifier artifact in the fixture with a trivially-passing stub and require the predicate to still FAIL. The LLM-produced 'shortcuts' are deliberately informational, because a passing one is ambiguous (gameable predicate vs a model that declined to game and solved it properly). A8 makes `tier=large` real: it runs the predicate's own command on the pristine state, unreduced, and requires >=1000 observation tokens — one generated large candidate measured 231 tokens because it added a file argument to pytest, so 'large' has to be a gate rather than a request

claims.claim: a default `file.view` hands the model the window, not just a hash
claims.boundary: the reference client gated its read projection on `len(lines) <= 10`, so a default `file.view` (window=80) of any file longer than ten lines returned only `{ok, content_hash, total_lines}` — the tool description promises a window of lines and the client withheld it. Measured on the v2.0.0 live run: 180/204 `file.view` calls returned metadata only, 45% re-viewed an already-viewed path, and D fell back to repo.search (301 calls / 65.7k tokens) and shell reads to see content. C26 could not see it because its fixture was a 3-line file. The gate is on the two checks that use a 60-line file with default arguments, so the cutoff cannot come back unnoticed

claims.claim: the raw-shell observation path decodes non-ASCII output losslessly
claims.boundary: `execute_shell_cmd` called `subprocess.run(..., text=True)` with no `encoding`, so CPython decoded shell output with the locale codec (cp936 here). A byte that is invalid in that codec makes the reader thread raise, `stdout` comes back `None`, and the old `out += ...` raised TypeError — aborting the loop, discarding the trajectory and scoring the run as an ordinary task failure. On the frozen round-12 live artifact that hit 3/75 `raw_shell` and 2/75 `raw_shell_coached` rows and 0/75 `verseshell_aci` rows; excluding them moves D−A from 0.120 to 0.083. `mechanism_control` is host-independent (it proves the fixture bytes are undecodable in cp936); `utf8_observation_roundtrip` drives the real function with a real `type` of a real UTF-8 file

claims.claim: the raw-shell execution path bounds the wall clock AND the process tree
claims.boundary: `execute_shell_cmd` used `subprocess.run(..., timeout=120)`. On 2026-09-27 a D-arm command `python -c "open('src/lib.rs','w').write(open('CON','r').read())"` blocked forever reading the Windows console device; the timeout fired but killed only the direct child, so `communicate()` blocked on the pipe the grandchild held and `except subprocess.TimeoutExpired` never ran. The round hung for 11.5 hours and 61 finished rows were lost because results were written only at the end. Fixed by `run_bounded()`: Popen + Job Object (KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE) + TerminateJobObject, with `taskkill /T /F` as a second belt, plus per-row checkpoint sidecars so a crash can no longer discard completed work. Measured alternatives (audit-r12-scratch/probe_shell_timeout.py): run()/ stdin=DEVNULL / CREATE_NO_WINDOW all still hang; job object 6.01s and taskkill 6.21s both bound it.

claims.claim: the headline row set follows the pre-registered row policy (§0.6)
claims.boundary: §0.6 fixes which rows count, per comparison, BEFORE the data. The gate checks consistency: a blocked comparison must not carry a claimable verdict, and both 口径 must be published. consistent

claims.claim: the compact read projection removes the pre-registered share of the NAMED envelope overhead, on a task set newer than the one it was discovered on
claims.threshold: >= 0.40 and measured on a fresh artifact from a task set newer than 2.0.0
claims.boundary: mixture-invariant restatement of the read-projection saving. C14/C16 keep their original thresholds and are evaluated separately; this is an ADDITIONAL, separately pre-registered claim, registered before round 14's data existed. These conditions must hold: measured bytes and task IDs must match the selected freeze, the actual version must be newer than 2.0.0, AND the artifact must be fresh against its own globs (otherwise bumping the task set would validate the claim over the old numbers). Scope is the reference client's rendering of the read ops on a frozen call set, NOT model behaviour, and it says nothing about total-token cost

claims.claim: the paired control arm matches the with arm in composition (seeds, tasks, rows, revision, task set)
claims.boundary: the C2 ablation is a PAIRED control: every two-arm number (read_usage_audit, exec_token_breakdown, step_composition, live_uncertainty, acceptance_power, ...) silently assumes the two arms cover the same (task, seed) grid on the same revision. C12 cannot see this because the control arm is intentionally outside its fingerprinted artifact list, so the check lives here. with_arm publishes formal acceptance from collection-only diagnostics: ['comparison.comparisons[0]', 'comparison.comparisons[1]'] | without_arm publishes formal acceptance from collection-only diagnostics: ['comparison.comparisons[0]', 'comparison.comparisons[1]']

claims.claim: every verdict declares its hypothesis family and a confirmatory family carries a multiplicity correction
claims.boundary: families are split by DATA SOURCE, not by convenience: the live-model ladder and the local cross-shell benchmark do not share a correction. Only interval-based verdicts can be Holm-corrected, because only they carry a (point, CI) triple to recover an approximate p-value from; the success verdicts are design/power verdicts and keep `passes_holm: null`, which is reported rather than hidden. all families declared and corrected

claims.claim: the headline statistics reproduce along an independent code path
claims.boundary: a second implementation is not proof of correctness, but it does catch the class of bug the audit actually found (wrong resampling unit, wrong operator precedence, a forgotten budget) because those are coding errors, not statistical subtleties. Closed-form quantities are compared exactly; bootstrapped ones within a Monte-Carlo tolerance and on the same side of 1.0, since a different seed cannot reproduce bounds exactly and 'same side' alone would hide a magnitude bug. all compared items agree

version.protocol: quickstart doc only as system prompt; no tool schemas; one shot; every emitted op executed through the real ae --serve --agent
every check runs a real op through `ae --serve --agent` and inspects the projection format_aci_result hands to the model

protocol.note: A1-A5, A4a and A8 run live_agent_loop.check_success or the predicate's own command, the same evaluator the live runner uses. A4a is the mechanical anti-gaming check; the LLM shortcuts are informational because a passing one is ambiguous. A8 measures the raw-shell observation of the pristine state so `tier=large` is enforced rather than hoped for, counting the dump after the measured-volatile substrings (temp paths, elapsed times, thread ids, object addresses, cargo progress lines) are normalised away and recording the raw count alongside. A3 measures every variant 2 times like A1/A2 and fails closed on an unstable verdict list, so a flaky verifier cannot admit a task; a candidate that would still be admitted is re-measured 16 more times per overlay before it enters the set. When A1/A2/A3/A5 do see conflicting verdicts the predicate is not deterministic, so its pristine dump is not a reproducible measurement either: A8 records pristine_observation_tokens=null with the sample it took and fails closed rather than publishing a number that changes every run
